passage: Tuesday. Chemistry again. I understood nothing of balancing equations, and half the class was finishing early. Jagdish Sir said, “Doubt? Come to my room at lunch.” I nodded and didn't go. If I go, he'll think I'm not clever enough, and Ritu, who sits ahead of me, will know. So I sat with the book in the library, drawing arrows. I've been doing this for three weeks. It's stupid. The next test is Friday, and I know I will fail equation balancing. My stomach is a stone. Asking feels like admitting I'm the weak one. But not asking has cost me everything I've tried. Maybe tomorrow I'll go to his room. Maybe. — Arohi

qa.q: Where did Jagdish Sir ask Arohi to come at lunch?
qa.a: Jagdish Sir asked Arohi to come to his room at lunch.

qa.q: Why did Arohi not go to Jagdish Sir's room?
qa.a: Arohi felt ashamed and afraid of being judged, sure that asking would mean admitting to being the weak one.

qa.q: What could Arohi do about the Friday test?
qa.a: Go to Jagdish Sir's room at lunch tomorrow with one specific equation and ask how to balance it.

qa.q: How might Jagdish Sir see students who do not come to his room?
qa.a: Jagdish Sir probably wants to help and would be glad to see Arohi, and may think a doubt is a normal thing to bring.

grounding: A teenager struggles alone with a subject because asking feels like admitting failure among peers who seem to understand.

passage:
Kamal: are you going to ask Ma'am about the pendulum problem?
Jeevan: no
Kamal: it's been three weeks, you keep saying you'll get it
Jeevan: everyone else gets it. if I ask it looks like I've been sleeping in class 😶
Kamal: no it doesn't. I asked about circuits last month
Jeevan: you're smart, it's different
Kamal: I'm not smart, I asked. that's the whole difference
Jeevan: hm
Jeevan: what if she says “you should know this by now”
Kamal: then you'll know she said it, and you still get the answer. coming to her table with me tomorrow?
Jeevan: ...maybe

qa.q: How many weeks has Jeevan been stuck on the pendulum problem?
qa.a: Jeevan has been stuck on the pendulum problem for three weeks.

qa.q: What is Jeevan afraid of about asking Ma'am?
qa.a: Jeevan is afraid of looking like someone who was sleeping in class and worries that Ma'am might say “you should know this by now”.

qa.q: What did Kamal say and do that made the request feel possible?
qa.a: Kamal shared having asked about circuits, said “I asked, that's the whole difference”, and offered to go to Ma'am's table together.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel about Jeevan's replies?
qa.a: Kamal is probably patient and caring, gently answering each fear while hoping Jeevan will say yes.

grounding: A teenager struggles alone with a subject because asking feels like admitting failure.
